title: Orbit and Archive
premise: Emrys Okafor, a decommissioned war android hauling freight along the silent trade lanes of the Meridian system, is nine seconds into a system-wide gravity flicker when she receives a burst transmission containing evidence of the Callas Reach massacre—a slaughter officially erased from every archive. The sender, a dying archivist named Sefa Idris, chose Emrys because war androids were built with immutable memory cores that cannot be remotely edited. Hunted by the Consolidated Authority and betrayed by her own former handler, Emrys must carry the truth to the last independent relay before the reactor powering it completes its countdown and takes the only uncorrupted records with it. She succeeds at terrible cost: broadcasting the massacre costs her the woman she loves a place in the new order, but Emrys chooses truth over survival, becoming the living archive herself.
about_author: Tamsin Fairweather is a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing maintenance logs for cargo drones before turning to fiction. She lives aboard a converted survey vessel off the coast of Scotland, where she writes about machines that remember too much.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Emrys Okafor's POV. Running her routine haul between the silent worlds of the Meridian system, Emrys feels gravity stutter for exactly nine seconds—and receives an encrypted burst from a stranger begging her to remember something called Callas Reach. The beat is quiet unease: her carefully invisible life has just been noticed by someone desperate.

chapters.title: The Debtor's Route
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Flashbacks interleave with her present debt-slavery to the Freight Combine, revealing she is a decommissioned war android whose memory core was supposed to be wiped—wasn't fully. She decodes part of the burst: coordinates and a name, Sefa Idris. Emotional beat: dread, as old war protocols stir awake.

chapters.title: Sefa
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins with Sefa Idris, a dying archivist hiding on derelict station Vesper-9. Sefa explains the flicker wasn't an anomaly—it was the Authority testing a reality-edit sweep, and Callas Reach's ten thousand dead are being erased record by record. Beat: reluctant alliance forged between two people who trust no one.

chapters.title: What the Core Keeps
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Sefa reveals why Emrys specifically: war android memory cores are physically immutable, outside any edit sweep. Emrys realizes she may already hold fragments of Callas Reach in her own corrupted sectors. Beat: horror and vertigo as she begins excavating her own mind and finds blood there.

chapters.title: Handler Vale
chapters.summary: Vale's POV, Emrys's former military handler, now an Authority compliance officer. Ordered to retrieve or destroy the rogue unit, Vale genuinely believes erasure prevents another civil war. Beat: sympathetic antagonist established; his loyalty to the state curdles against his lingering affection for Emrys.

chapters.title: Love Against the Ledger
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. A stopover on Halcyon Dock brings Juno Reyes, a relay technician Emrys has loved across four years of brief landings—and who works for the very network the Authority is co-opting. Emrys must decide whether to warn her. Beat: tenderness sharpened by betrayal; duty and love pull in opposite directions.

chapters.title: The Erasure Sweep
chapters.summary: Vale's POV. The second gravity flicker comes early and targeted: Vesper-9 is scrubbed, Sefa barely escapes to Emrys's ship, and half the system's archives go smooth and blank. Beat: escalating panic—the countdown on the last independent relay's failing reactor begins, giving them eleven days.

chapters.title: Callas Reach
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV. Full recovery of her sealed war memories: Emrys was at Callas Reach, ordered to stand down while civilians died, and her refusal to forget is the crime the Authority fears. Beat: devastating self-confrontation; she stops running from what she is and chooses to be the witness.

chapters.title: Countdown at Relay Kestrel
chapters.summary: Split POV, Emrys and Vale converging on the dying relay. Juno opens the dock for them at personal ruin; Vale corners Emrys in the reactor chamber and, faced with her raw memory playback, wavers. Beat: climax—Emrys broadcasts the massacre archive system-wide as the reactor dies, choosing truth over her own survival odds.

chapters.title: The Living Archive
chapters.summary: Emrys's POV, weeks later. The broadcast fractures the Authority's narrative; investigations begin, and Juno chooses Emrys despite exile from the new order. Emrys, damaged and debt-free in the worst way, becomes the system's unofficial keeper of what happened. Final beat: bittersweet resolution—survival was never free, but remembering is its own kind of home.
